blocks.text: 1. Caching
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448058798-469759378.png

Human Evaluation closed the Evaluation module by validating automated metrics against real human judgment. Caching, storing and reusing the result of an expensive step instead of recomputing it, opens this dedicated Production RAG module by naming the first and most general technique for running a RAG pipeline efficiently at real scale.
Caching checks a cache first, and only does the real work when nothing usable is already stored.
2. A Request This Production RAG Module Covers From Here On
Every pattern covered earlier in this course assumed a working, well built pipeline.
This Production RAG module instead covers what keeps that pipeline running reliably at real scale.
3. Caching Trades Storage For Repeated Compute
Re-running the exact same expensive operation for the exact same input wastes real compute.
Storing that result once and reusing it trades storage space for saved compute time.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","What is spent"],"rows":[["No caching","Repeated compute on every identical request"],["Caching","Storage space, saved compute on repeat requests"]]}

blocks.text: 4. A Cache Key Must Identify The Request Uniquely

blocks.alt: A Cache Key Must Identify The Request Uniquely
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448058798-129420366.png
A cache key must capture everything that could change the correct result.
A key missing a relevant input risks returning a stale result for a different request.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A cache key built from only the query text returns the same cached answer even if the underlying document set changed since it was cached, exactly the risk of a key missing a relevant input.

blocks.text: 5. Cache Hits Versus Cache Misses
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448058798-813669626.png
A cache hit returns the stored result immediately, skipping the expensive work entirely.
A cache miss falls through to doing the real work, then stores the result for next time.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Outcome","What happens"],"rows":[["Cache hit","Stored result returned immediately"],["Cache miss","Real work runs, then the result is stored"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Stale Data Breaks The Value Of Caching

blocks.alt: Stale Data Breaks The Value Of Caching
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448059298-172678574.png
A cached result that no longer reflects reality is worse than doing no caching at all.
Caching needs its own invalidation strategy, not just storage.
7. Cache Eviction When Storage Fills Up

blocks.alt: Cache Eviction When Storage Fills Up
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448059298-336000045.png
A cache cannot grow forever, so old or rarely used entries eventually need to be evicted.
An eviction policy decides exactly which entries get removed when space runs out.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A least-recently-used eviction policy removes the entry that has gone the longest without being accessed, a common default choice when a cache reaches its storage limit.

blocks.text: 8. What Specifically To Cache In A RAG Pipeline

blocks.alt: What Specifically To Cache In A RAG Pipeline
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448059299-158792057.png
Nearly every stage of a RAG pipeline is itself a distinct, cacheable operation.
Embedding cache and response cache, covered next in this module, are the two most impactful places to apply this idea.
9. Recognizing When Caching Is Worth Adding To A Stage

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Caching Is Worth Adding To A Stage
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448059299-699714399.png
A stage receiving the same or similar inputs repeatedly benefits from caching.
A stage where every input is unique, by contrast, gets little benefit from caching.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates a minimal cache with hit and miss handling and least-recently-used eviction.

code.content:
from collections import OrderedDict

class SimpleCache:
    def __init__(self, max_size=3):
        self.store = OrderedDict()
        self.max_size = max_size

    def get(self, key):
        # return the cached value and mark it as recently used
        if key in self.store:
            self.store.move_to_end(key)
            return self.store[key]
        return None

    def set(self, key, value):
        # evict the least-recently-used entry once the cache is full
        if key in self.store:
            self.store.move_to_end(key)
        self.store[key] = value
        if len(self.store) > self.max_size:
            evicted_key, _ = self.store.popitem(last=False)
            print(f"Evicted: {evicted_key}")

def expensive_operation(query):
    return f"Result for: {query}"

def cached_call(cache, query):
    # normalize the query into a cache key
    cache_key = query.lower().strip()
    result = cache.get(cache_key)
    if result is not None:
        return f"[cache hit] {result}"
    result = expensive_operation(query)
    cache.set(cache_key, result)
    return f"[cache miss] {result}"

cache = SimpleCache(max_size=2)
print(cached_call(cache, "What is the Falcon plan?"))
print(cached_call(cache, "What is the Falcon plan?"))
print(cached_call(cache, "What is the Eagle plan?"))
print(cached_call(cache, "What is the pricing page?"))

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the second identical query returning a cache hit instantly, and the third distinct query eventually evicting the oldest entry once the cache exceeds its max size.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Building a cache key that omits an input that actually affects the correct result.
Caching results with no invalidation strategy, letting stale data persist indefinitely.
Letting a cache grow without bound instead of defining an eviction policy.
Adding caching to a stage where nearly every input is unique.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Caching stores and reuses the result of an expensive step instead of recomputing it.
This Production RAG module covers what keeps a working pipeline running reliably at scale.
Caching trades storage space for saved compute time on repeated identical requests.
A cache key must capture everything that could change the correct result.
A cache hit returns the stored result immediately; a cache miss does the real work and stores it.
A cached result that no longer reflects reality is worse than no caching at all.
An eviction policy decides which entries get removed when the cache runs out of space.
Nearly every stage of a RAG pipeline is a distinct, cacheable operation.
